RANDO PABRUA PACIS Punong Barangay Barangay San Juan Sur Municipality of Manabo Province of Abra Dear PB Pacis: This has reference to your letter dated 30 October 2024 seeking this Department's legal opinion regarding the Sangguniang Barangay member who incurred absences without justifiable reasons and attended the regular session while under the influence of alcoholic beverages. Per your representation, you alleged that Sangguniang Barangay Member Shanie Dela Rosa Mina incurred absences without justifiable reasons for four regular sessions enumerated as follows: February 18, 2024; April 7, 2024; July 7, 2024; and October 6, 2024. You then represented that on April 21, 2024, during the regular session, you alleged that Ms. Mina attended the session even though she was under the influence of alochol. You stated that you pleaded with her and threatened to remove her from the session if she continued to attend while under the influence of alcohol. Thus, you are requesting this Department's legal opinion on what particular case should be filed or disciplinary action to be instituted against the alleged erring kagawad. Foremost, since the official concerned is a member of the Sangguniang Barangay (SB) of San Juan Sur, then the Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) of the SB is applicable to him. However, in such application of the IRP in this case, please be guided by Section 50 of RA 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) which provides: "Section 50. Intemal Rules of Procedure. (a) On the first regular session following the election of its members and within ninety (90) days thereafter, the sanggunian concerned shall adopt or update its existing rules of procedure. (b) The rules of procedure shall provide for the following: (5) The discipline of members for disorderly behavior and absences without justifiable cause for four (4) consecutive sessions. for which "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

they may be censured. reprimanded. or excluded from the session. suspended for not more than sixty (60) days. or expelled: Provided. That the penalty of suspension or expulsion shall require the concurrence of at least two-thirds (2/3) vote of all the sanggunian members: Provided, further, That a member convicted by final judgment to imprisonment of at least one (1) year for any crime involving moral turpitude shall be automatically expelled from the sanggunian; and (6) Such other rules as the sanggunian may adopt. (Emphasis supplied) Absences regarding the frequency provided under the Local Government Code is contingent on justifiability to be actionable administratively. 1 As a result, SB Member Mina can be reprimanded in accordance with the provisions of your IRP, given that your letter made no mention of SBM Mina's absences during four (4) consecutive sessions. Given the absence of such evidence, the action to be taken against the accused erring SB Member should be based on the IRP adopted by the Sanggunian. Please note, however that the IRP should not be in conflict with the provisions of the LGC and other relevant laws, otherwise, the LGC will prevail.2 Regarding the allegations that SB Member Mina attended the session while under the influence of alcohol, Section 60 (c) of the LGC may be the basis for administrative culpability, to wit: "Section 60. Grounds for Disciplinary Actions. - An elective local official may be disciplined, suspended, or removed from office on any of the following grounds: (c) Dishonesty, oppression, misconduct in office, gross negligence, or dereliction of duty; xxxx" (Emphasis supplied) Further, in the case of Ombudsman u Espina3, the Supreme Court defined what the term "misconduct" means, viz: "Misconduct generally means wrongful, improper or unlawful conduct motivated by a premeditated, obstinate or intentional purpose. It is intentional wronqdoinq or deliberate violation of a rule of law or standard of behavior and to constitute an administrative offense the misconduct should relate to or be connected with the performance of the official functions and duties of a public officer. It is a transgression of some established and definite rule of action, more particularly, unlawful behavior or gross negligence by a public officer. There are two (2) types of misconduct, namely: grave misconduct and simple misconduct. In grave misconduct, as distinguished from simple 1 DILG Opinion No. 69 S. 2019, October 14, 2019 2 Ibid 3 G.R. No. 213500, March 15, 2017 Page 2 of 3

misconduct, the elements of corruption, clear intent to violate the law, or flagrant disregard of an established rule must be manifest. Without any of these elements, the transgression of an established rule is properly characterized as simple misconduct only." (Emphasis ours) Based on the foregoing, an administrative case for Simple Misconduct under Section 60 of the LGC may be filed against SB Member Mina for attending sessions while under the influence of alcohol, which is a deliberate violation of a Sangguniang Bayan Member's standard behavior during regular sessions. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P.
